transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-06 15:30 PT
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO - Stratus), Maya (Head of Infra), Luke (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on whether Stratus AI should adopt Redwood Dedicated (private nodes) vs Redwood Hosted fallback for peak bursts. Key topics: reserved pool sizing, tenant isolation/topology, burst prewarm strategies, expected scaling timeline, security/KMS, and a 3-day benchmark proposed.

Topics:
- Current infra: latency SLOs, models in scope (LlamaX-70B and two finetunes), traffic patterns
- Isolation: per-tenant node vs soft multi-tenant with fencing and warm-pools
- Burst: cold-start vs prewarm, warm pool sizing, fallback to hosted API
- Cost tradeoffs: reserved monthly commit vs pay-for-burst on hosted fallback

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: all right hey everyone thanks for making time. this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our systems engineer. how's everyone?
[00:08] Alex: yeah hey thanks, sorry bit of a crazy morning, all good on our side.
[00:12] Maya: hi all. quick note, we're joining from our SFO office.
[00:16] Jordan: great. super quick agenda, want to understand your traffic, isolation requirements, and what burst looks like so we can map to reserved capacity or private nodes.
[00:22] Priya: and i'll follow up with specific benching ideas and the warm-pool configs we usually recommend.
[00:27] Luke: sounds good, we're evaluating three paths: fully hosted, dedicated reserved, or private with VPC peering. leaning toward dedicated but want to see isolation guarantees and cost.
[00:37] Alex: our primary constraint is 99th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts, and < 800ms for long-form summarization. throughput spikes to ~180 rps for autocomplete during release windows, sustained baseline ~30 rps.
[00:52] Priya: ok that's helpful — rough question on models, are you running larger context sequences? what model sizes?
[00:58] Luke: main one is LlamaX-70B-FT for completions and a 13B finetune for intent classification. typical token lengths are 30–80 for autocomplete and 800–1,200 tokens for summaries.
[01:12] Jordan: got it. for 70B at that throughput you typically need multiple GPU devices in pool; reserved capacity is likely the right call to hit SLO without blowing egress costs.
[01:23] Maya: can you explain the isolation options? we need tenant-level data separation for compliance, not necessarily physical dedicated HW per tenant but logical isolation is must.
[01:32] Priya: sure — we offer a couple patterns. one is private nodes (VPC + private control plane) where the customer controls networking and KMS; another is dedicated reserved fleet with node fencing so workloads are pinned and KV caches are tenant-scoped. the difference is in control and egress: private nodes give you full VPC peering and no shared control plane egress.
[01:50] Alex: how does warm-pool prewarm work? last time we saw big latency spikes because caches were cold.
[01:56] Priya: two layers — prefix/KV caching at the runtime and warm pool prewarmed instances. warm-pool is a set of pre-initialized model workers that keep KV cache hot for frequent prompts. you can size warm-pool as percentage of peak concurrency — we typically recommend 10–25% as starting point.
[02:12] Luke: 10–25% seems broad. for our traffic we want prewarm ready for ~50 concurrent long summaries during releases. what's the cost?
[02:19] Jordan: cost will be reserved commitment plus a small warm-pool delta. i'll send a detailed math for 4 vs 8-GPU equivalent reserved pools.
[02:26] Maya: can Redwood auto-burst to hosted when we exceed reserved? we don't want dropped requests.
[02:31] Priya: yes — smart routing can overflow to hosted-compatible variants automatically and we maintain token routing so you get degraded model versions but no hard failures. note that dual paths add egress and potentially higher per-token rates during overflow.
[02:45] Alex: how fast is the overflow? like if we see a sudden jump from 30 to 180 rps can it failover within seconds?
[02:51] Priya: the routing decision is sub-second for new requests, but warm-pool spin-up for private nodes might take 20–90s depending on model initialization. that's why prewarm and small hot pools are recommended. for immediate spikes we route to hosted as fallback.
[03:07] Luke: curious about cache warming persistence — if we move from hosted to private, do we lose cached KV?
[03:12] Priya: KV cache is local to a serving pool. we can replicate prefix caches on controlled handoffs in the bench, but cross-environment cold cache is a known limitation; we mitigate by overlapping warmers.
[03:23] Jordan: there's also quantized model variants for lower-cost burst handling — 8-bit or 4-bit quantized versions that run faster but may have slight quality diffs.
[03:33] Alex: our product owners will push back on quality drift. how much degradation have you seen?
[03:37] Priya: depends on model and eval set. for some finetunes 8-bit has <2% regression on ROUGE/BLEU style metrics; for 4-bit you might see 3–6% on sensitive tasks. we recommend validating with your eval prompts.
[03:53] Maya: security — we need KMS integration and audit logs for token access. is that included in private?
[03:58] Jordan: private includes KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we also provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:06] Alex: any caveats for VPC peering? we run egress NAT gateways with strict egress policies.
[04:11] Priya: we can peer, but traffic patterns matter. path MTU, DNS, and NAT rules come up a lot. we also need outbound port allowances for the control-plane heartbeat. we can share a checklist.
[04:23] Luke: bench specifics — we'd like a 3-day run with typical ramp and synthetic spikes, measure p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and failover behavior. can Redwood provision a temporary burst add-on?
[04:33] Priya: yes, we can provision a timebox bench in our dedicated cluster or we can replicate your VPC in private staging. for quick results dedicated cluster is faster.
[04:41] Jordan: we'll propose two options: 1) quick dedicated bench using Redwood infra with your prompts, and 2) private VPC mirrored bench which takes longer to set up but closer to production network constraints.
[04:54] Alex: timing — we aim to decide on a vendor and POC by end of May. what's realistic to get bench data for decision?
[05:00] Priya: if you share prompts and traffic profile by next Monday (May 9), we can run bench May 11–13 and deliver results by May 14 for you to review.
[05:10] Maya: licensing / contract qs — do reserved commits have cancellation windows if usage changes?
[05:14] Jordan: contracts are flexible; standard is a 12-month commit with options to scale at quarter boundaries. we'll include different term pricing and ramp plans in the spreadsheet.
[05:24] Luke: do you support bringing our own keys to HSM? we have strict key custody requirements.
[05:29] Priya: yes, BYOK to HSM is supported for private deployments. for dedicated we can integrate with your KMS as well, with appropriate key wrapping.
[05:37] Alex: any performance tuning knobs we should know about? e.g., KV cache TTL, batching windows, sequence length cutoffs?
[05:43] Priya: yep — autoscaling windows, adaptive batching thresholds, and max sequence cutoffs are all knobs. we typically tune batching based on observed latency percentiles; small batching windows help low-latency but reduce throughput efficiency.
[05:56] Maya: what about multi-region? we need EU data residency for some customers, and US for others — can Redwood split fleets by region and route?
[06:03] Jordan: yes, region-based routing is supported. you can pin customers to region-local fleets and have cross-region fallback if allowed.
[06:09] Alex: ok that covers the big topics. do we have any open items?
[06:12] Jordan: recap — Jordan sends pricing + security pack; Priya schedules bench and prepares bench sheet; Luke to provide prompts and traffic profile; Maya to confirm VPC peering constraints. propose SE deep-dive for next Tuesday.
[06:26] Alex: that works. thanks everyone.
[06:29] Maya: thanks.
[06:30] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional misheard model names (LlamaX transcribed as Llama-10X in first pass), KV cache sometimes 'KV cash', and timing markers are approximate.
